Steady State by Pseudo-Transient Continuation

Source: R/ptc.R
ptc.Rd

Solves \(f(x, p) = 0\) for variables of a cppFUN() model, one output per solved variable, optionally under linear constraints \(C x = total\). flow = TRUE follows the ODE flow to a stable steady state; flow = FALSE returns any regular root. The result depends only on the start, the parameters and the controls.

Usage

ptc(
  fun,
  x,
  parms,
  solve = names(x),
  rows = solve,
  C = NULL,
  total = NULL,
  flow = TRUE,
  positive = TRUE,
  controls = list()
)

Arguments

fun

A compiled cppFUN() object with forward derivatives.

x

Named numeric, values of all variables of fun. The solved variables start there, the others keep their values.

parms

Named numeric, values of the parameters of fun.

solve

Names of the variables to solve for. Default all.

rows

Names of the outputs of fun paired with solve, in the same order. Default solve.

C, total

Constraint matrix with columns named by solve, and the right-hand side: C x = total. Default none.

flow

Logical, default TRUE: the outputs are the right-hand side of an ODE. FALSE for plain equations.

positive

Logical, default TRUE. Keep the solved variables positive; they must start positive.

controls

Named list:

  • reltol (default 1e-10) and abstol (1e-14): each residual is measured against reltol times the turnover \(\sum_k |\partial f_i / \partial x_k|\, |x_k|\) plus abstol times the largest Jacobian entry of the residual. Newton steps from there, while they contract, bring each variable to within reltol * (abs(x) + abstol) of the root.

  • flowTol (1): relative local error of a pseudo-time step.

  • maxit (400): maximum number of iterations of one descent; a continuation from an unstable root starts another.

  • dtInit (1e-2): the first pseudo-time step, relative to the fastest rate if flow = TRUE.

  • zmax (5): the largest change of the logarithm of a variable per step.

  • stability (TRUE): with flow = TRUE, a root must be stable on the kernel of C. From an unstable root the search continues along the unstable direction, first to the side the iterates came from.

  • stabilityTol (0): with stability, a root counts as stable while the real part of the leading Jacobian eigenvalue on the kernel of C is at most stabilityTol. A small positive value accepts a state that leaves the root more slowly than a time scale of interest, such as near a Hopf bifurcation.

Value

A list with the named solution x (all variables), converged, iterations and message.

References

Kelley CT, Keyes DE (1998). Convergence analysis of pseudo-transient continuation. SIAM J Numer Anal 35(2):508-523.

See also

cppFUN()

Examples

# \donttest{
if (codegenAvailable()) {
  ## Enzyme E converts S to P, P returns to S. E + ES and S + ES + P are
  ## conserved, so the steady state is fixed by the two totals.
  f <- c(E  = "-kon * E * S + (koff + kcat) * ES",
         S  = "-kon * E * S + koff * ES + kback * P",
         ES = " kon * E * S - (koff + kcat) * ES",
         P  = " kcat * ES - kback * P")
  enz <- cppFUN(f, variables = names(f), parameters = c("kon", "koff", "kcat", "kback"),
                modelname = "ptc_enzyme", outdir = tempdir(), compile = TRUE)
  C <- rbind(Etot = c(E = 1, S = 0, ES = 1, P = 0),
             Stot = c(E = 0, S = 1, ES = 1, P = 1))
  ss <- ptc(enz, x = c(E = 1, S = 1, ES = 1, P = 1),
            parms = c(kon = 1, koff = 0.5, kcat = 0.3, kback = 0.1),
            C = C, total = c(1, 10))
  ss$x
  enz$func(E = ss$x[["E"]], S = ss$x[["S"]], ES = ss$x[["ES"]], P = ss$x[["P"]],
           kon = 1, koff = 0.5, kcat = 0.3, kback = 0.1)
}
# }
